key_big: Build new facts from ones you know: 6 is 5 + 1, 7 is 5 + 2, 8 is double 4 and 9 is 10 − 1.
body_html:
Multiplication is equal groups

7 × 6 means 7 groups of 6. In an array, it is 7 rows with 6 dots in each row. You can turn it round: 6 × 7 is the same, 42.

Build new facts from facts you know

You already know the tables of 2, 4, 5 and 10. Use them.

In the table of 9, the two digits always add up to 9: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81.

Division facts

Division is the inverse of multiplication. Three numbers make a fact family: 6 × 8 = 48, 8 × 6 = 48, 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6.

Example

63 ÷ 9 = ?

Think: 9 × ? = 63. 9 × 7 = 63.

Answer: 7

Word problems: draw a model

Draw equal units. Find 1 unit by dividing, or many units by multiplying.

Times as many

Ali has 7 marbles. Siti has 6 times as many. How many marbles does Siti have?

1 unit = 7. 6 units = 6 × 7 = 42.

Answer: 42 marbles

faq.q: When do children learn the multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9 in Singapore?
faq.a: In Primary 3. The tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 come in Primary 2, and the tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9, with their division facts, come in Primary 3.

faq.q: How can I help my child remember 7 × 8 and 6 × 9?
faq.a: Build them from easier facts: 7 × 8 = 5 × 8 + 2 × 8 = 40 + 16 = 56, and 6 × 9 = 6 × 10 − 6 = 54. Children often mix up 56 and 54, so practise these two side by side.

faq.q: What is a fact family in P3 maths?
faq.a: A fact family is the 4 facts made from 3 numbers, such as 6 × 8 = 48, 8 × 6 = 48, 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6. It shows that division is the inverse of multiplication.

faq.q: Are the tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9 in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics syllabus has the multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9, multiplying and dividing within the tables and mental calculation in Primary 3. Students use these facts every year up to the PSLE.

sets.title: Tables of 6 and 7: arrays and skip counting

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 6 dots in each row. 4 × 6 = 24. Count in 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 7 dots in each row. 3 × 7 = 21. Count in 7s: 7, 14, 21.

items.q: Which multiplication does this number line show?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the marks: there are 5 jumps of 6 from 0 to 30. So 5 × 6 = 30. 6 × 6 counts the 0 as a jump.

items.q: Which multiplication does this number line show?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the marks: there are 4 jumps of 7 from 0 to 28. So 4 × 7 = 28. 5 × 7 counts the 0 as a jump.
There are 6 rows with 7 dots in each row: 6 × 7 = 42. 6 + 7 only adds the two numbers.
6 rows of 8 is 5 rows of 8 and 1 more row of 8: 40 + 8 = 48. 41 adds 1, not one more row of 8.

items.q: 5 × 6 = 30 and 2 × 6 = 12. What is 7 × 6?
items.e: 7 rows of 6 is 5 rows and 2 more rows: 30 + 12 = 42. 36 is only 6 rows (6 × 6).

items.q:
Count in 6s. What comes next?
18, 24, 30, ?
items.e: Each number is 6 more than the one before: 30 + 6 = 36. So 6 × 6 = 36.

items.q:
Count in 7s. What comes next?
28, 35, 42, ?
items.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before: 42 + 7 = 49. So 7 × 7 = 49.

items.q:
Count in 7s. What is the missing number?
7, 14, ?, 28
items.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before: 14 + 7 = 21. So 7 × 3 = 21.
6 × 7 is 5 × 7 and one more 7: 35 + 7 = 42.
6 × 6 is 5 × 6 and one more 6: 30 + 6 = 36.
6 × 4 is 5 × 4 and one more 4: 20 + 4 = 24.
6 × 3 is 5 × 3 and one more 3: 15 + 3 = 18.

items.q: Which number is in the multiplication table of 7?
items.e: The multiplication table of 7 goes 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70. 49 is in the list (7 × 7).

items.q: Which number is not in the multiplication table of 6?
items.e: The multiplication table of 6 goes 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60. 26 is not in the list.

sets.title: Tables of 8 and 9: doubling and patterns

items.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Double it to find 8 × 6.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 6 is double 4 × 6: 24 + 24 = 48.

items.q: 4 × 9 = 36. Double it to find 8 × 9.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 9 is double 4 × 9: 36 + 36 = 72.

items.q: 10 × 4 = 40. Take away one 4 to find 9 × 4.
items.e: 9 groups is 1 group less than 10 groups. 40 − 4 = 36. 39 takes away 1 instead of one 4.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Take away one 8 to find 9 × 8.
items.e: 9 groups is 1 group less than 10 groups. 80 − 8 = 72. 79 takes away 1 instead of one 8.

items.q: In the table of 9, the tens digit is one less than the number you multiply by, and the two digits add up to 9. Use this to find 9 × 7.
items.e: The tens digit is one less than 7, so it is 6. The ones digit makes the sum 9: 6 + 3 = 9. So 9 × 7 = 63.

items.q: In the table of 9, the tens digit is one less than the number you multiply by, and the two digits add up to 9. Use this to find 9 × 6.
items.e: The tens digit is one less than 6, so it is 5. The ones digit makes the sum 9: 5 + 4 = 9. So 9 × 6 = 54.

items.q: Look at the table of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The tens digit goes up by 1 each time. What happens to the ones digit?
items.e: The ones digits are 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. Each one is 1 less. Adding 9 is adding 10 and taking away 1.

items.q:
Count in 8s. What comes next?
32, 40, 48, ?
items.e: Each number is 8 more than the one before: 48 + 8 = 56. So 8 × 7 = 56.

items.q:
Count in 9s. What comes next?
45, 54, 63, ?
items.e: Each number is 9 more than the one before: 63 + 9 = 72. So 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 9. 4 × 9 = 36. Count in 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 8. 5 × 8 = 40. Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40.
9 × 9 is 10 × 9 take away one 9: 90 − 9 = 81.
9 × 5 is 10 × 5 take away one 5: 50 − 5 = 45.
10 groups of 9 is 9 tens: 10 × 9 = 90. 19 adds instead of multiplies.
9 × 3 is 10 × 3 take away one 3: 30 − 3 = 27. 72 has the digits the wrong way round.

items.q: Which number is in the multiplication table of 9?
items.e: The multiplication table of 9 goes 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90. 81 is in the list (9 × 9).

items.q: Which number is not in the multiplication table of 8?
items.e: The multiplication table of 8 goes 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80. 46 is not in the list.

items.q: Which multiplication fact helps you find 63 ÷ 9?
items.e: Division is the inverse of multiplication. 63 ÷ 9 asks: 9 times what makes 63? 9 × 7 = 63, so 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

items.q: Which multiplication fact helps you find 56 ÷ 8?
items.e: Division is the inverse of multiplication. 56 ÷ 8 asks: 8 times what makes 56? 8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

items.q: 54 counters are put into groups of 9. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 6 groups of 9. 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Check: 6 × 9 = 54.

items.q: 40 counters are put into groups of 8. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 5 groups of 8. 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Check: 5 × 8 = 40.

items.q: How many jumps of 7 does it take to go from 35 back to 0?
items.e: Count the jumps: 35, 28, 21, 14, 7, 0 is 5 jumps. So 35 ÷ 7 = 5. 6 counts the marks instead of the jumps.

items.q: 7 × 8 = 56. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so 56 ÷ 7 = 8 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 56.

items.q: 9 × 6 = 54. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so 54 ÷ 9 = 6 and 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Division starts with the biggest number, 54.

items.q: Mei Ling writes 7 ÷ 63 = 9. What should she write?
items.e: She divided the wrong way. Start with the total, 63, and divide it by 7: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Check: 7 × 9 = 63.

items.q: Wei Ming writes 6 ÷ 48 = 8. What should he write?
items.e: He divided the wrong way. Start with the total, 48, and divide it by 6: 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 6 × 8 = 48.
Ask: 6 times what makes 42? 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42, so ? = 7.
Ask: 7 times what makes 63? 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Check: 7 × 9 = 63, so ? = 9.
Ask: 8 times what makes 56? 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 7.
Ask: what times 9 makes 54? 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Check: 6 × 9 = 54, so ? = 6.
Ask: what times 6 makes 48? 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 8 × 6 = 48, so ? = 8.
Ask: what times 8 makes 72? 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Check: 9 × 8 = 72, so ? = 9.
Use the inverse: ? = 6 × 7 = 42. Check: 42 ÷ 7 = 6. 13 only adds the numbers.
Use the inverse: ? = 8 × 9 = 72. Check: 72 ÷ 9 = 8. 17 only adds the numbers.
Ask: 56 ÷ what makes 7? Think 7 × ? = 56. 7 × 8 = 56, so ? = 8.
Ask: 54 ÷ what makes 9? Think 9 × ? = 54. 9 × 6 = 54, so ? = 6.

items.q: Which fact is in the fact family of 7, 9 and 63?
items.e: The fact family is 7 × 9 = 63, 9 × 7 = 63, 63 ÷ 7 = 9 and 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 63.

items.q: A fact family uses the numbers 8, 9 and ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: The biggest number in a multiplication fact family is the product: 8 × 9 = 72. 17 is 8 + 9.

items.q: A fact family uses the numbers 6, 9 and ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: The biggest number in a multiplication fact family is the product: 6 × 9 = 54. 15 is 6 + 9.

items.q: 9 × 6 = 54, 6 × 9 = 54 and 54 ÷ 9 = 6. What is the fourth fact in this fact family?
items.e: The last fact divides 54 by the other number, 6: 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Always start with 54.
You can multiply in any order: 7 × 8 and 8 × 7 are both 56. So ? = 7.

items.q: Ryan says 7 × 8 = 54. What is the correct answer?
Raju says 6 × 9 = 56. What is the correct answer?

items.e: 9 × 7 is one more group of 9 than 9 × 6. So add 9: 54 + 9 = 63. Adding 7 or 1 does not add a whole group of 9.

items.q: 8 × 6 = 48. Use this to find 8 × 7.
items.e: 8 × 7 is one more 8 than 8 × 6: 48 + 8 = 56. 55 adds 7 instead of 8.
7 × 6 is one group of 7 less than 7 × 7. So take away 7: 49 − 7 = 42. Taking away 6 or 1 does not take away a whole group of 7.

items.q: Mdm Wong bakes curry puffs. She puts 6 curry puffs on each tray. She bakes 8 trays. How many curry puffs does she bake?
items.e: 8 trays of 6: 8 × 6 = 48. 14 is 8 + 6, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are there in 9 weeks?
An octopus has 8 arms. There are 6 octopuses in a tank. How many arms are there altogether?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48. 40 is only 5 octopuses.

items.q: At the hawker centre, each table has 6 stools. Ethan counts 7 tables. How many stools are there?
For Sports Day, there are 8 teams. Each team has 7 students. How many students are there?
items.e: 8 × 7 = 56. 54 is a common mistake: 54 is 6 × 9.

items.q: Sarah reads 6 pages of her library book each day. How many pages does she read in 9 days?
items.e: 9 days of 6 pages: 9 × 6 = 54. 56 is 7 × 8, not 6 × 9.

items.q: Jun Jie gets 9 red packets at Chinese New Year. There is $8 in each red packet. How much money does he get?
A bowl of noodles costs $6. Chloe buys 4 bowls for her family. How much does she pay?
items.e: 4 × $6 = $24. $10 is 4 + 6, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Mrs Lim shares 56 stickers equally among 8 pupils. How many stickers does each pupil get?
items.e: 8 units = 56. 1 unit = 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56. 48 takes away 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: Mr Tan cuts a rope 63 m long into 7 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 7 units = 63 m. 1 unit = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 m. Check: 7 × 9 = 63.

items.q: 72 students stand in rows of 9 for assembly. How many rows are there?
items.e: 72 ÷ 9 = ? Think 9 × ? = 72. 9 × 8 = 72, so there are 8 rows.

items.q: 54 mandarin oranges are packed in bags of 6. How many bags are there?
items.e: 54 ÷ 6 = ? Think 6 × ? = 54. 6 × 9 = 54, so there are 9 bags.

items.q: Xin Yi saves $9 each week. How many weeks does she take to save $63?
items.e: 63 ÷ 9 = ? 9 × 7 = 63, so it takes 7 weeks.

items.q: 48 chairs are set out at the void deck in 6 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 = ? 6 × 8 = 48, so there are 8 chairs in each row.

items.q: Kumar has 7 marbles. Kavya has 6 times as many marbles as Kumar. How many marbles does Kavya have?
items.e: 1 unit = 7. 6 units = 6 × 7 = 42. 13 is 6 + 7, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Hui Min has 8 stickers. Zhi Hao has 9 times as many stickers as Hui Min. How many more stickers does Zhi Hao have than Hui Min?
items.e: Zhi Hao has 9 units and Hui Min has 1 unit. The difference is 8 units: 8 × 8 = 64. 72 is how many Zhi Hao has, not how many more.

items.q: Siti has 49 beads. She has 7 times as many beads as Nurul. How many beads does Nurul have?
items.e: 7 units = 49. 1 unit = 49 ÷ 7 = 7. Nurul has 7 beads. 56 multiplies instead of divides.

items.q: Devi buys 6 packets of stickers. There are 8 stickers in each packet. She gives away 5 stickers. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48. Then 48 − 5 = 43. 48 forgets the 5 stickers given away.

items.q: Farah has 9 boxes of crayons with 7 crayons in each box. She also has 4 loose crayons. How many crayons does she have altogether?
items.e: 9 × 7 = 63. Then 63 + 4 = 67. 63 forgets the 4 loose crayons.

items.q: A plate of kaya toast costs $4 and a drink costs $2. Priya buys 8 plates of kaya toast and 8 drinks for her friends. How much does she pay?
items.e: Each plate and drink costs $4 + $2 = $6. 8 × $6 = $48. $32 is only the kaya toast.
